issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() in Farm.java, but both the template and the solution define and use a method named singFarmSong() instead. This name mismatch between the specification and the provided code can confuse students about which method to implement and could cause mismatch with tests or instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() (preferred, since template and solution use that name), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong() so it matches the specification and UML. Ensure accompanying documentation and example Main usage are updated accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatch (printFarmSong vs. singFarmSong) names the same conceptual operation with different identifiers across artifacts and can confuse students about which method to implement and test.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() (preferred, matching template/solution), or rename the template/solution method to printFarmSong() so all artifacts use the same identifier.
